title: How Much Does It Cost to Pressure Wash a House? [2026 Data]
summary: Need to breathe new life into your dirty siding and trim? Explore the cost to pressure wash a house to boost your curb appeal instantly.

Cost Insights:


-


Professional pressure washing for your house costs between **$0.10** and **$0.50** per square foot depending on the area you need cleaned.


-


The number of stories in your home and the type of material being cleaned determine how much labor your project requires.


-


Budget for add-on services like soft washing for roofs, concrete sealing, or gutter cleaning when you schedule your pressure washing appointment.


-


[Hiring a local power washing professional](https://www.angi.com/nearme/power-washing/) prevents damage to your siding and window seals for a cleaner finish.


In 2026, the national average cost to pressure wash a house is **$312** , based on 51,092 verified projects reported by Angi Pros. Most homeowners pay between **$213** and **$449** , with the final cost determined by the area being cleaned, the number of stories, and the type of surface. If you're pressure washing an entire home rather than a single surface like a driveway or patio, expect your total to land toward the higher end of that range.


## House Pressure Washing Cost by Square Foot: What to Expect


Pressure washing costs **$0.10 to $0.50 per square foot** , depending on which part of your property you're cleaning, with flat and easily accessible surfaces like driveways and patios sitting at the lower end. Because a technician still pays for gas, insurance, and other overhead regardless of project size, the per-square-foot rate drops when you give a professional more area to cover. Here's how pressure washing costs break down by home size:


Home Size (Square Feet) Average Cost in 2026


1,500 $150–$750


2,000 $200–$1,000


2,500 $250–$1,250

## House Pressure Washing Cost by Project Type


Pressure washing costs vary widely depending on which area of your property you're cleaning. The table below breaks down average pressure washing costs for different types of projects:


Pressure Washing Project Average Cost Range in 2026


Driveway $100–$250


Patio $100–$200


Fence $150–$300


Gutters $50–$150


Roof $450–$700


Siding $150–$1,400


One-story house $150–$750


Two-story house $400–$1,400


Three-story house $700–$1,800


### Driveway


The[cost to pressure wash a driveway](https://www.angi.com/articles/cost-to-pressure-wash-driveway.htm) runs **$100 to $250** on average, or **$0.20 to $0.40 per square foot** , though larger or dirtier driveways can push the total up to **$500** . Driveways with heavy motor oil buildup require[pressure washing with bleach or a less abrasive cleaning solution](https://www.angi.com/articles/bleach-alternative-for-pressure-washing.htm) , along with additional labor, which raises the final cost.


### Patio or Deck


Having a professional[pressure wash a deck](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-to-power-wash-deck.htm) or patio costs **$100 to $200** , with the final price shaped by the size of the surface, the material, and how easy it is to access. Stairs, obstructions, or surfaces that require reduced pressure to avoid damage will add time and push your cost toward the higher end of that range.


### Fence


Pressure washing a fence costs **$150 to $300** , with the price driven by the fence's length and material. Wood fences require lower pressure and a more careful technique than PVC or metal fences, so they typically take longer and cost more to clean.


### Gutters


[Pressure washing your gutters](https://www.angi.com/articles/clean-gutters-with-pressure-washer.htm) costs **$0.50 to $1.50** **per foot** , which works out to **$50 to $150** for a single-story home. For taller homes, a technician will need a ladder or bucket truck to[clean the gutters](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-much-does-gutter-cleaning-cost.htm) , which adds to your overall project cost.

### Roof


Marina Lohrbach / iStock Photography / Getty Images


Pressure washing a roof costs **$0.50 to $1.00 per square foot** , or **$450 to $700** overall, making it one of the pricier pressure washing projects. The elevated cost reflects the difficulty of getting equipment onto the roof, navigating sloped terrain, and the safety gear required to do the job safely.


### Siding Only


Pressure washing siding alone costs **$150 to $1,400** on average, though large projects can reach **$2,500** , depending on the amount of surface area to be cleaned. Even this focused project can make a noticeable difference in your home's curb appeal.


## House Pressure Washing Costs by Story: How Height Affects Price


The number of stories in your home directly affects pressure washing costs, since two- and three-story homes require a ladder, scissor lift, or bucket truck that adds to your total. The table below breaks down average pressure washing costs by the number of stories:


Number of Stories Average Pressure Washing Cost in 2026


One $150–$1,000


Two $400–$1,400


Three $700–$1,800


## Cost to Pressure Wash by House Material


The material your home is made of influences pressure washing costs because some surfaces require specialized cleaning techniques that take more time and labor. Here’s how house material affects pressure washing costs per square foot:


House Material Average Cost per Square Foot in 2026


Brick $0.10–$0.40


Stucco $0.30–$0.50


Wood $0.30–$0.55


Vinyl $0.20–$0.50


### Brick


[Pressure washing brick](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-to-pressure-wash-brick.htm) costs **$0.10 to $0.40 per square foot** on average, making it one of the more affordable materials to clean. Despite brick's durability, pros follow careful practices to protect the mortar and avoid discoloring the masonry.


### Stucco


[Cleaning stucco](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-clean-stucco.htm) costs **$0.30 to $0.50 per square foot** and requires a gentle approach, since removing dirt and grime from the ridged surface takes extra time and care.


### Wood


Pressure washing wood costs **$0.30 to $0.55 per square foot** , and wood's porous nature means professionals often need to[soft wash](https://www.angi.com/articles/soft-wash-better-regular-pressure-washing.htm) wooden siding, fences, and decks to prevent damage.


### Vinyl


Pressure washing vinyl costs **$0.20 to $0.50 per square foot** , and while vinyl tolerates more water pressure than stucco or wood, pros still use specific techniques to avoid cracking the material.

## House Pressure Washing vs. Power Washing Costs: Which Is Pricier?


Pressure washing and power washing are often used interchangeably, but they differ in method and cost, with power washing typically costing more due to the use of heated water. Here are the differences between the two methods:


Pressure Washing Power Washing


Less expensive More expensive


Uses cold water Uses hot water


Best for fences and decks that don’t have stubborn stains Best for walkways and patios that have tougher dirt and grime


Lower risk of damaging surfaces Potential risk of damage or burns from hot water


## How Often Should You Pressure Wash Your House?


You should aim to pressure wash your home once per year, and the best time is between March and November in most areas. These months rarely have temperatures that dip too low, which risks freezing the water or damaging the machines. That said, demand is higher in the spring and summer, so you could experience longer wait times for a professional to come (and possibly higher costs).


Here’s how often you should pressure wash different areas of your home:


Area of Home Best Time to Pressure Wash Reason


Siding Spring or fall Mild temperatures, less risk of mold and mildew buildup


Driveway Spring or fall After winter snow or fall leaves to remove debris and grime


Deck or patio Late spring and end of summer Prepare outdoor spaces for summer use and clean up after peak season


Roof Late spring or early fall Prevents moss growth and removes debris before harsher weather


## Why You Should Hire a Pressure Washing Pro


Jodi Jacobson / E+ / Getty Images


Almost the entirety of the cost of hiring a professional for pressure washing services will go toward labor, which means you stand to save an average of over $300 if you DIY. However, it’s important to have a solid understanding of what pressure to use on different materials to avoid damage, as well as what areas you shouldn’t pressure wash to avoid leaks. Hiring a[power washing company near you](https://www.angi.com/nearme/power-washing/) to get the job done is well worth the small investment.


### Here’s why it’s ideal to hire a pressure washing pro


In theory, pressure washing a house is a simple and straightforward task, but in practice, there are a few important upsides to hiring a pro you should consider:


-


Professionals know what pressure to use on different materials to prevent damage to siding, roofing, and more.


-


Pros can often point out issues with rotting wood, damaged fascia boards, and other materials that require repair that a DIYer might miss.


-


DIY mistakes can lead to damage to siding, window frames, and door frames, as well as water leaks if you accidentally damage window and door seals.


-


Professionals are more likely to get an even clean that maximizes curb appeal and home value.


## How You Can Save Money While Pressure Washing


When hiring a[pressure washing company near you](https://www.angi.com/nearme/power-washing/) , the following tips can help save money.


-


The price per square foot often decreases when you have a larger project. As such, consider scheduling a “bulk” pressure washing of several areas of your property, such as your driveway, patio, and siding.


-


Get quotes from at least three contractors to find the best price.


-


Schedule pressure washing during the off-season, like early spring or late fall, when prices might be lower.


-


Regularly maintain your property to prevent the buildup of heavy dirt, grime, mold, and mildew. This might eliminate the need for an expensive deep clean.


-


Consider tackling smaller or more straightforward projects yourself, making sure to follow all safety guidelines. Save on pressure washer rental costs by going in with a friend or neighbor.


Next Steps: Finalize Your Project With a Pro


-


Be prepared to discuss your home size, number of floors, and home layout with your pro.


-


Mention what materials you have on or around your home that you want pressure washed.


-


Ask your pro if they use cleaners and ensure they’re safe for use around plants and pets, if applicable.


-


Discuss any add-on services you want, like soft washing for your roof, concrete sealing, or gutter cleaning.

Frequently Asked Questions


It usually takes about two to four hours to pressure wash a 2,000-square-foot home. The exact time depends on how much dirt there is, the type of siding, and whether you’re doing it yourself or hiring a[professional pressure washing service](https://www.angi.com/nearme/power-washing/) . A DIY job can take an average of six to eight hours, but you should plan for it to take an entire day. A pro can get the job done quicker.


When hiring a professional to pressure wash your home, it's crucial to choose a company that is bonded, licensed, and insured. This protects you from liability if any accidents or property damage occur during the service; otherwise, the cost could fall on you. Before making a decision, vet at least three different contractors. Conduct thorough research by reading customer reviews, looking at examples of their previous work, and verifying the company's license. Before signing a contract, ensure you receive a written estimate that details all project costs. It's also wise to ask potential contractors a series of questions to gauge their professionalism and experience, such as:


-


How many years of experience do you have?


-


What are your credentials?


-


What cleaning methods do you use?


-


Do you have a workmanship warranty and insurance?


-


What is your availability?


-


What is your policy if you damage my property?


-


How long will the job take to complete?


-


How much do you charge?


-


What is your cancellation policy?


-


Do you offer a customer satisfaction guarantee or any additional services?


Depending on the amount of experience you have with power washing or pressure washing, hiring a professional is likely a better option.[Using a pressure washer](https://www.angi.com/articles/how-to-use-pressure-washer.htm) requires a bit of know-how to avoid damaging siding, trim, roofing shingles, and even the seals on your windows. Holding the pressure washer too close to the material you’re cleaning can cause damage to the surface. You can wash your home’s exteriors with a garden hose, but high-pressure cleaning should be done by professionals.
